title: SSO: IdP-specific claim mapping recipes and ingress behaviors (Okta/Azure/Google/Ping)
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Deliver a set of IdP-specific SAML attribute/claim mapping recipes and ingress behavior notes for Okta, Azure AD, Google Workspace, and Ping. These recipes will be used by platform engineers and SREs to configure customer IdP integrations and by the product team to improve onboarding guides. Focus is on deterministic RBAC v2 mappings, group handling, NameID formats, audience/recipient validation, and safe defaults for audit logging.
acceptance_criteria: A1: One-line attribute/claim recipe exists for each IdP describing the canonical attribute names and an example SAML assertion we accept.
A2: Examples for mapping SAML attributes to RBAC v2 roles are provided and validated in the integration test harness.
A3: Audit logging requirements documented: what fields we record, retention classification, and redaction rules for PII in assertions.
A4: Playbook sections for common customer misconfigurations (group prefixes, email vs principalName mismatch, multiple NameIDs) with remediation steps.
A5: Automated tests (integration + unit) reference to PR and passing CI in branch accompanying this ticket.
A6: Security review requested and noted with next steps (if any).
compatibility_recipes: Okta (recommended): attribute sources: Use 'groups' for team/group membership, 'user.email' or 'email' for primary identity, and a custom 'redwood_roles' attribute when customers want role-based role assertions. NameID format: urn:oasis:names:tc:SAML:1.1:nameid-format:emailAddress. Audience: https://inference.redwood.ai/saml/acs. Signature algorithm: RSA-SHA256. Common gotchas: Okta may include full group paths ("engineering/product/redwood"); recipe recommends 'strip_prefix=1' by default to keep last path segment. Example assertion snippet: Subject->NameID=email@example.com; AttributeStatement->Attribute(name="groups")->Value("eng-core").

Azure AD (recommended): attribute sources: use 'http://schemas.xmlsoap.org/ws/2005/05/identity/claims/name' or 'preferred_username' for login; groups may be sent as 'groups' claim or via Graph API (overage handling). NameID: urn:oasis:names:tc:SAML:1.1:nameid-format:emailAddress or transient depending on tenant. Audience: app's entityID configured in Azure. Notes: Azure can return group object IDs instead of names when group claims exceed the limit; recipe includes fallback to call Microsoft Graph in Dedicated/Private deployments to resolve IDs when allowed. Example mapping: map group object IDs to RBAC role via 'groupId->role' lookup table stored in config.

Google Workspace (recommended): attribute sources: 'email' as NameID is most reliable. Groups: Google often uses 'groups' claim only in SAML Add-On configs; otherwise, SCIM/group-sync is recommended. NameID format: emailAddress. Special behavior: Google always signs assertions with SHA256 and uses long cert rotation windows; recipe includes certificate rotation checklist for customers. Example: map 'primaryEmail' -> user principal and 'isAdmin' custom attribute for superuser mapping.

Ping (recommended): attribute sources: PingFederate/PingOne often use 'memberOf' or 'groups' and can provide nested group structures. NameID formats: support both persistent and emailAddress. Important: Ping sometimes sends multi-valued attributes as a single semicolon-delimited string in older adapters; recipe provides parser toggles that split on ';' and on header 'X-Ping-MultiValue=true'. Audience and recipient checks are strict; note recommended SP configuration to accept 'Recipient' header values. Example mapping: AttributeStatement->Attribute(name='roles')->Value('platform-admin,infra-lead') and parser splits into two RBAC roles.

General Sizing/Performance notes: For high-volume customers, configure 'group_sync' off by default and rely on SAML group assertions or SCIM for regular sync; enable assertion caching and TTL to reduce auth spikes. For Dedicated deployments, enable optional Graph/SCIM resolution only when customers approve outbound calls.
rbac_mapping_examples: Example A - Simple mapping (Okta groups -> RBAC): SAML groups: ["eng-core", "eng-oncall"] => RBAC v2: {"project:eng": ["viewer"], "infra:oncall": ["operator"]} (rule: group name -> resource prefix mapping using 'group_prefix_map').

Example B - Attribute-based roles (Azure AD claims): Claim 'redwood_roles' = 'admin,storage_reader' => map directly to RBAC roles admin + storage_reader. Rule: prefer explicit 'redwood_roles' over groups when present.

Example C - Email-to-org fallback (Google): If groups are absent, derive org from email domain (e.g., 'acme.com') and apply 'org:acme:member' role with least privilege. This is opt-in and documented in onboarding playbook.

Example D - Group ID resolution (Azure overage): If Azure returns object IDs for groups, use optional 'group_id_map' config to translate IDs to names. For on-prem/private customers we recommend using SCIM instead of resolution calls.
audit_logging_notes: Minimum audit fields recorded for every SAML login: timestamp, assertion ID, NameID (hashed for PII-sensitive configs), incoming Assertion issuer (IdP entityID), selected principal email (if available), final RBAC roles granted, mapping reason (explicit claim vs group fallback vs email-domain), relayState, ACS URL, and certificate fingerprint used to verify signature. Redaction rules: raw assertion.Body is written to secure audit bucket only when customer opts-in for troubleshooting; otherwise store a redacted assertion with attribute names but hashed values. All audit logs must follow retention classification 'security:30d' unless enterprise retention is configured. Log entries must include trace_id to correlate with token issuance and API request logs.
test_plan: TP1: SP-initiated login end-to-end for each IdP using canonical recipe (automated): validate NameID -> user link, RBAC mapping, and audit log entry created.
TP2: IdP-initiated login flow (manual + automated smoke): ensure correct relayState handling and role mapping across NameID changes.
TP3: Group-overflow (Azure) simulation: return >150 group claim and validate fallback to Graph resolution and mapping via group_id_map. Verify dedicated opt-in behavior.
TP4: Multi-value attribute parsing (Ping) with semicolon-delimited attribute; validate parser toggles and unit tests cover edge cases with whitespace and empty values.
TP5: Certificate rotation: rotate IdP certs twice and validate graceful acceptance within rotation window and failure outside window with clear admin-facing error messages.
TP6: RBAC regression tests: when mapping rules change, run promptset and authorization test harness to ensure no privilege escalations (automated CI gate).
TP7: Audit log privacy test: verify hashed NameIDs and redaction behavior for customer that opted out of raw assertions.
